label: text
text:
TRANSPORTERS' LICENCES
TO BE CANCELLED?

label: text
text: PROTEST OVER SEARCH.

label: text
text: Canton's "new" boycott comes into force to-day, Nov. 8, but it is not known if the threat to British ships will be carried out until a few days later.

label: text
text: The Transport Union (cargo toolies and curgo boats) in Canton has refused to handle shipments on the fleets of the Steamböat Co., the Indo-China S.N. Co. and the China Navigation Co.

label: text
text:
Nevertheless, the s.s. "Liang-chow" (China Navigation) has brought down some cargo, en route for Shanghai.
From a reliable source the "China Mail" learns that the Maritime Customs authorities in Canton will cancel the licences of those concerned should cargo not be worked.

label: text
text: An association has been formed to clamour for the abrogation of Treaties and this is very active at the moment.

label: text
text: With regard to Canton's inspection corps to search all shipping, the "Cantor" Gazette reported that a number of Consuls had acquiesced. Such is not the case.

label: text
text: On October 23, the Consular Body in Canton pointed out that the Customs were the only body authorised to carry out searches on vessels.

label: text
text: Later on, the Portuguese Consul (as doyen), on behalf of the Consular Body, protested against the examination, in reply to Mr. Eugene Chen's despatch of Oct. 20.

label: text
text: Strike Headquarters Gutied on Saturday.

label: text
text: Damage to the extent of about $100,000 was done on Saturday when the Strike headquarters at East Garden were gutted in a fire lasting two hours.

label: text
text: A considerable quantity of goods confiscated during the boycott was burned out.

label: text
text: Conflicting reports are to hand with regard to the hundred or so unfortunate prisoners, detained for alleged offences against the Strike regulation.

label: text
text: Some say that all the prisoners were marched out, those on longer terms of imprisonment being sent to the Police department while others were released. A few escaped in the confusion.

label: text
text: Three European style buildings were damaged and the many matshed “departments” were destroyed.

label: text
text: Armed police and pickets restored order after trouble had threatened to break out.

label: paragraph_title
text: WINDING UP.

label: paragraph_title
text: KWONG CHOW HOTEL CO'S AFFAIRS.

label: text
text: APPLICATION GRANTED.

label: text
text: An application was made in the Supreme Court this morning for the winding-up of the Kwong Chow Hotel Co., Ltd., of 578, Queen's Road, West.

label: text
text: Mr. C. G. Alabaster K.O., (instead by G. K. Hall Brutton and Co.) made the application, which was on the debtor company's own petition.

label: text
text: The petition, said Mr. Alabaster, stated that the Company was incorporated in May, 1922 with its registered office at 578, Queen's Road West and a capital of $100,000 divided into 1,000 shares. In the course of carrying on restaurant and hotel business debts had been contracted to the extent of $26,500, all of which were overdue and the Company was unable to meet them.

label: text
text:
Two meetings of shareholders had been called but owing to insufficiency of numbers it had been found impossible to pass a resolution in favour of a voluntary winding-up order being made. The Company was unable to continue business and although an offer had been made for the purchase of the business as a going concern which would amount to considerably more than that of the debts, this offer would be withdrawn if the goods were sold in execution. The bailiff was already in possession in connection with a judgment debt for $7,000.
The winding-up application order was granted with the continuance of the special manager already provisionally appointed.

label: paragraph_title
text: Y.M.C.A. NOTES.

label: paragraph_title
text: WEEK'S SPORT AND LITERARY ACTIVITIES.

label: text
text: RAMBLE ARRANGED

label: text
text:
Of primary importance this week is mention of the first Ladies' Night of the winter. This took place last Thursday, at 9 p.m., after some fifty guests had salt down to dinner at tastefully decorated tables.
The programme was an excellent one, and varied. Mr. Grenham was very humorous, as usual, and Mrs. Fleming gave delightful renderings of Easthope Martin's Songs of Old London, Miss McGill, pleased the Scots members of the audience, and also all the rest, by her singing of Scots songs and Mr. Arrowsmith in a particularly gruesome effort entitled 'Murders' succeeded in causing great amusement, especially among the golfing frater.

label: text
text: The Y.M.C.A. Quartette was heard for the first time, and sang some old English songs very well Messrs. Petrie and Sands gave a short sketch, a skit on F. Anstey's Play. 'Vice Versa.'

label: text
text: The competition, without which Ladies" Night would not be complete, was in the form of pictorial representations of well known books, "Tom Sawyer" and "A Gentleman of Courage" creating much amusement.

label: text
text: Last Tuesday, the Y.M.C.A. played its first game of "hockey against the Club 2nd XI." After a good game, we lost to the Club by 2 goals to 3. Not a bad effort for our first essay. We had better results on Saturday when the the Y.M.C.A. Bowlers met the K.B.G.C. In this game we managed to beat our opponents. 87 shots to 69, and feel highly pleased with ourselves in consequence.

text: we are playing a match with the K.G.C. at Kowloon City. This will also be the occasion of the official opening of the new club house, so altogether a very enjoyable day is promised.

text: It is hoped within the next few days to add some more new volumes to the library, to bring it up to date.

text: The many friends of Mr. A. W. Ingram will be pleased to hear that he is now out of hospital, and hopes very shortly to be talking up work again.

label: text
text: The Study Circle will begin on Wednesday week, at 6.30 p.m. in Room 24, and a hearty invitation is extended to all members.

label: text
text: We hear that the new tennis courts are progressing favourably, and will be playable in about a month's time, so members are asked to possess their souls in patience, as we want the courts to be in first class condition. The time of opening will be announced as soon as conditions allow.

label: paragraph_title
text: "WAS SENSELESS."

label: paragraph_title
text: BUT WILL FIND WAY TO PRISON.

label: text
text: A POLICE DESERTER.

label: text
text: A former member of the Hong Kong Police Force was brought before Mr. R. E. Lindsell at the Central Magistracy this morning to answer a charge of desertion.

label: text
text: Capt. H. F. Bloxham, A.S.P., conducting the case for the Police, said that on Dec. 14 last the defendant applied for admittance to hospital as he was sick. He never went to hospital but left for Weihaiwei where he enlisted in the Police. He had been traced and brought from Weihaiwei to Hong Kong to answer the present charge. His wife and children had been sent back to Wei-hai-wei at Government expense.

label: text
text: His Worship: Why did you run away?—I was senseless. I found myself on board the ship. I do not know how I got there.

label: text
text: Mr. Lindsell: You will now find your way to prison—six months.

label: paragraph_title

label: paragraph_title
text: ONE JAILED, ANOTHER BOUND OVER.

label: text
text: Two Chinese young women who described themselves as actresses were charged before Major C. Willson at the Central Magistracy this morning with the theft of a quantity of jewellery and silk, together with the sum of $178 in cash, the property of the mistress of one of the accused. After hearing evidence in support of the charge, His Worship bound over the younger of the two defendants and sent the elder to prison for one month with hard labour.

label: paragraph_title
text: ALLIES TO MAKE ANOTHER STAND?

label: text
text: CANTON MOVÉS, UP.

label: text
text: No new development of importance, as regards the war in North China, has been reported during the week-end.

label: text
text: Marshall Sun Chuan-fang, after losing his base at Kiukiang, is reported—to be re-assembling his troops at Wukau, also on the southern bank of the Yangtse river, further back than Kiukiang; but in front of Anking (capital of Anhui province) and Nanking.

label: text
text: About 1,600 Allied troops, under Chow Feng-chi, went over to the Cantonese while their comrades made a vain effort to stand their ground.

label: text
text: Other Southern detachments are moving up to reinforce the small body holding Kiukiang but it is not expected that the Northerners will counter-attack just yet.

label: paragraph_title
text: TREACHERY AGAIN

label: paragraph_title
text: Factor In Canton's Capture of Kukiang.

label: text
text: On Friday the "China Mail" stated that treachery would have played a part in the unexplainable fall of Kiukiang. A week-end cable reads:—

label: text
text: Shanghai, Nov. 6

label: text
text: The latest reports from Kiukiang show that treachery again had "a big part in the Northern defeat, a number of Chekiangites refusing, it is believed by orders of their officers. to join Sun Chuan-fang's loyal troops to defend the city against 2,000 Southern attackers.

label: text
text: There was much firing on the native city, but no casualties in the foreign concessions.

label: text
text: It is known that the Northerners intended to counter-attack but otherwise there is no confirmation of a Japanese report that the North-erners have reoccupied Kiukiang.—Reuter.

text: Final Objective.

label: text
text: Shanghai, Nov. 6.

label: text
text: Northern troops are retreating to Nanking.—Reuter.

text: [Note: Nanking is the capital of Kiangan province (in which Shanghai is also situated) and is the seat of Marshal Sun Chuan-fang's government.

label: paragraph_title
text: CANTON'S CLAIMS

label: paragraph_title
text: Report That Troops Are Neur

label: text
text: Canton, Nov. 0.

label: text
text: Reports received here to-day indicate general improvement in the Yangtse campaign.

label: text
text: The capture of Kliukiang by Cantonese forces has been verified by several sources, although details are lacking.

label: text
text: The general situation in Hupch indicates "that the entire province is under Nationalist control."

label: text
text: The unification of Hunn province, politically and militarily, is proceeding smoothly.

label: text
text:
The Fukien campaign is also progressing. Cantonese troops being near Foochow, the provincial capital.
As regard Yunnan, the military head of that province is sending an emissary to Canton to negotiate submission to the Nationalist Government.

label: text
text:
In Kwangtung, the provincial authorities are drafting plans to make of it a "model province". The plan includes the creation of an institute for training civil service officials; the establishment of a peasants' bank to relieve labour conditions; and the organisation of four army divisions to make a final cleanup of bandits in the interior.
- Canton Information Bureau

text: [Note: There is no confirmation of Canton's claim to be "near Poochow". As reported in the "China Mail," the Nationalists have won signal success in Fukien.

label: paragraph_title
text: STILL HOPE.

label: text
text: COAL PARLEY'S AGAIN TO-DAY

label: text
text: OPTIMISM RESTRAINED

label: text
text: Rugby, Nov.: 7.

label: text
text: No definite results emerged from yesterday's long conversations on the coal dispute at the Prime Minister's residence, but the parleys are to be resumed tomorrow.

label: text
text: In view of past disappointments, optimism is restrained, but it is generally agreed that the situation has taken a more hopeful turn.

label: text
text: There was not a joint meeting between the parties to the dispute yesterday, each side meeting the Prime Minister and certain other members of the Cabinet separately.

label: text
text: An official statement issued later gave no indication of the trend of the conversations which were based on proposal submitted by the miners through the mediation, in the first instance, of the Trades, Union Council.

label: text
text: Some modification of these proposals was, it is understood, suggested by the owners, and was placed before the miners.

label: text
text: After consultation with the Trades Union Council, the miners decided to consider the owners' suggestions, which it is assumed have reference to the national principles which it is proposed should govern district agreements.

label: text
text: A "meeting of the Miners' Executive has been called to examine the proposals to-morrow morning, and in the early afternoon the miners' representatives will resume their conversations with the Prime Minister.

label: text
text: It seems probable that the discussion will extend over the next two or three days, and it is anticipated that the Miners' Executive will recall the delegates for a meeting in London this week, so that they may be kept in touch with the progress of the negotiations.—British Wireless Service.

label: paragraph_title
text: COOK'S OUTBURST.

label: paragraph_title
text: "I Will Never Sign."

label: text
text: Startling declarations were made by Mr. Cook at Liverpool. "I see no sign of peace in the coal dispute. The levy brings £50,000 a week and we shall win if we have the silver bullets."

label: text
text: Mr. Cook added that he will not accept the conditions offered at any price, not even to save himself or his organisation. "I will never sign an agreement meaning a longer working day and reduction of the standard of living. Establishment of district settlements will not bring peace."—Reuter.
